newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cocoa prices dip, shadow New York fall.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cocoa prices dip, shadow New York fall.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices edged down on Thursday in line with declines in New York futures overnight and on uncertainty over a move to halt trade in unfermented beans in a key producing area, traders said.
They said cocoa was quoted at 2,750-80 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 2,810-20 a week ago.

"The market is slowing following overnight falls in New York," one trader said. "Another reason is that some exporters have been putting off purchases because of the regulation issued by the (South Sulawesi) governor."
The governor decreed that there should be no trade in unfermented cocoa beans in South Sulawesi. He said all parties involved in buying cocoa should stop purchasing unfermented beans.
Traders said only about 10 percent of the bean trades in South Sulawesi were fully fermented to the required five days.
"Some exporters are a little confused about what to do," one trader said. "So, they have temporarily stopped buying. This is one reason why prices have been easing."
Another trader said farmers were unlikely get premium prices even if they fermented their beans.
Another trader said he was buying as usual because he considered partially fermented beans would meet the governor's ruling, aimed at improving the quality of beans being traded.
"As far as I am concerned, it's business as usual. Whether the beans are fermented for two days or five, I consider them fermented," he added.
The traders also said that the mid-crop harvest was beginning to slow, keeping the market quiet.
They said arrivals in South Sulawesi were estimated at 16,800 tonnes in August, 17,330 tonnes in September and 22,000 tonnes in October.
